scope: Proposition 4.2 of the manuscript “Elliptic squares and Zilber–Pink for curves in A2” (preprints/Elliptic-Squares-and-Zilber-Pink-for-Curves-in-A2-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 016 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d3ecf115570d0b89), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 20. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: After one fixed finite cover of the curve in Proposition 3.1, there are distinct fixed odd primes ℓ1, ℓ2 and a fixed lift of the center t0 with the following properties. Every non-CM elliptic-square target on the previous curve has a lift t for which, in the respective marked five-spaces, Πt0,ℓ1 + Πt,ℓ1 is a degenerate four-space, (4.2) Πt0,ℓ2 + Πt,ℓ2 is a nondegenerate four-space. (4.3) The prime ℓ1 divides none of the fixed Hecke multipliers in Proposition 3.4. The prime ℓ2 is different from every residue characteristic at which the fixed center is not potentially good. Both center-plane reductions are nondegenerate. The conditions remain valid upon simultaneous conjugation of all the data, and the degree of any chosen lift increases by at most a fixed factor.
